chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 86 — The Stars Descend and Violent Offspring Arise
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest extant Aramaic witness, 4QEnochᶠ (4Q207), fragment 1, lines 1–5, for its surviving portions of 1 Enoch 86:1–3; the early Greek witness P.Oxy. XVII 2069, fragments 1r–2r, for its surviving portions of 86:1–2; and the complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann’s 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, printed page 62, for the full six-verse chapter and all wording absent from the fragments. Where the early witnesses preserve only broken words or lines, their lacunae were not treated as surviving text; the complete Geʽez witness supplies the wording. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no text absent from the primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: Again I saw with my own eyes while I was asleep. I saw heaven above, and look, one star fell from heaven. It rose and ate and grazed among those cattle.
verses.study: The first falling star enters the world represented by cattle and shares their pasture. Within the vision’s symbolism, a heavenly being has crossed into the human realm and begun the disorder recalled from the Watchers’ descent.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–2 — heavenly beings cross a boundary and take human women
1 Enoch 6:1–6 — the Watchers descend and bind themselves to their plan

verses.text: Then I saw the large black cattle. Look, all of them exchanged their pens, their grazing grounds, and their calves, and they began to live with one another.
verses.study: The exchanging of pens, pasture and young portrays the collapse of established boundaries. The oldest surviving Aramaic wording points to living together, while the Geʽez textual tradition reads their action as crying out to one another; both stand within a scene of corrupted order.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:2 — the sons of God take women from humankind
Jude 6 — angels abandon their proper place and are kept for judgment

verses.text: Again I saw in the vision and looked toward heaven. Look, I saw many stars descend and cast themselves down from heaven beside that first star. Among those calves they became cattle, and they grazed with them in their midst.
verses.study: The single descent becomes a multitude. The stars’ transformation into cattle makes their intrusion visible within the vision’s earthly symbolism and shows many heavenly beings joining the first in his transgression.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:4 — the transgression involves the sons of God and the daughters of humankind
1 Enoch 6:6–8 — the Watchers descend together and their leaders are named

verses.text: I looked at them and saw that all of them exposed their sexual organs like horses and began to mount the female cattle. They all conceived and gave birth to elephants, camels, and donkeys.
verses.study: The vision speaks plainly about illicit unions and represents their offspring as three kinds of oversized or unusual animals. The varied creatures are not a celebration of strength; they embody the unnatural result of the heavenly beings’ rebellion.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:4 — mighty offspring arise from the forbidden unions
1 Enoch 7:1–2 — the women conceive and bear destructive giants

verses.text: All the cattle were afraid of them and were terrified before them. The new creatures began to bite with their teeth, devour, and gore with their horns.
verses.study: Fear spreads as the offspring turn their strength against the cattle. Teeth and horns make the violence concrete: corruption that began with a breached boundary now becomes predation against the earth’s inhabitants.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:11–13 — the earth becomes corrupt and filled with violence
1 Enoch 7:3–5 — the giants consume, oppress and turn against living creatures

verses.text: Then they began to devour those cattle. Look, all the children of the earth began to tremble and shake before them and to flee.
verses.study: The chapter closes with the whole earthly community recoiling before the devourers. Unrestrained violence destroys security and drives the vulnerable away, preparing for the earth’s cry and heaven’s answer in the next movement of the vision.
crossReferences: Genesis 6:12–13 — universal corruption brings the earth under divine judgment
Habakkuk 1:2–3 — violence and destruction provoke a cry for God to act

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 86 continues the Animal Vision by retelling the rebellion of the Watchers. Stars represent heavenly beings, cattle represent humanity, and the stars’ descent into the cattle’s pastures depicts the crossing of a boundary between heaven and earth.

The first star is joined by many others. Their shared grazing and their unions with the female cattle show that the rebellion is both corporate and embodied: heavenly beings deliberately enter a realm and relationship not appointed to them.

The elephants, camels and donkeys born from these unions symbolize offspring whose existence disrupts the created order. Their violence reveals the moral fruit of the rebellion. Power detached from obedience becomes predatory, and its first victims are those among whom it seeks to live.

The chapter’s theological movement is from trespass to fear, violence and flight. It teaches that created boundaries are gifts under God’s rule, that communal sin multiplies its effects, and that the suffering of the earth’s children calls for divine judgment and rescue.

crossReferences: Genesis 6:1–4 — heavenly beings, human women and mighty offspring
Genesis 6:11–13 — corruption and violence fill the earth
1 Enoch 7:1–6 — their offspring consume and terrorize life
Jude 6 — angels leave their appointed dwelling and await judgment
Habakkuk 1:2–3 — violence gives rise to a cry for justice
